tools.name: extract_claims
tools.description: Split a text (for example an AI-generated answer) into atomic factual claims, each with its character span and a grounding_required flag that says whether it is a checkable fact (questions, greetings and opinions are flagged false). Use it before verify_claim to decide what to check. Price: $0.05 US

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Check one factual claim against public Wikipedia sources and return a verdict (supported, contradicted, outdated, mixed or insufficient_evidence), a confidence score, a short reason, the supporting quote and the source URL. Says insufficient_evidence instead of guessing. Price: $1.00 USDC on Base pe

tools.name: check_answer
tools.description: Fact-check a whole answer: extracts every checkable claim and verifies each one against public Wikipedia sources, returning a verdict, confidence, quote and source URL per claim plus suggested next actions. Use it to audit chatbot or RAG output before showing it to a user. Price: $1.00 USDC on Base

tools.name: deep_verify
tools.description: Multi-source verification of up to three claims in a text against Wikipedia, Wikidata, Google News, Europe PMC (PubMed studies), FRED (US economic data) and SEC EDGAR (US company filings). Returns verdict, confidence, evidence for and against with quotes and URLs, and flags contradiction when source

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: extract_claims, verify_claim, check_answer, deep_verify · Public sink: extract_claims, verify_claim, check_answer, deep_verify.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: extract_claims, verify_claim, check_answer, deep_verify · Public sink: extract_claims, verify_claim, check_answer, deep_verify

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
